Part 2 is R itself and the IDE in which you write it. The R tutorial is worked live, a slide at a time, the IDE follows in six steps on the screen of the facilitator, and the part ends with a session of your own on the panel, in the browser lab or in your IDE. The part takes ninety minutes.

## 1. The R tutorial

**On the slides.** Ten slides are typed along: R in one slide, getting data in, inspecting the data, and working with rows and columns. The tutorial goes on to model formulas, fixed effects with fixest and reading what comes back, and ends on plotting with tinyplot, causal graphs in R and the error messages that you are most likely to meet. Type each block in an editable cell of the browser lab, or in the console of your IDE.

[Open the browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

To go further: [Getting started with R](../../companion/intro-r.qmd), whose first steps are in the [module of the same name](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds-housing/companion/intro-r.html) on the housing-audit site.

## 2. The IDE, step by step

**On the slides.** The facilitator opens the folder of the workspace, runs the check, reads the panel and views it, filters the view, draws one figure and renders the report. With the workspace, follow in your IDE. Otherwise follow on the shared screen and do the middle three steps in the browser lab.

To go further: [Positron, RStudio and VS Code](../../companion/ide.qmd).

## 3. Hands-on 2 – R on the panel

[Open the browser lab at Task 2](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-2-get-the-data-and-look-at-it){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

In an editable cell of Task 2, or in the working script of the workspace, peek at the panel, keep one country and three columns, summarise the result by year, and draw one figure. Then change one thing in each step and read what comes back.

**By the end of the part** you have read a data frame, filtered it, summarised it and drawn it in R, and you know where each of these happens in an IDE.
